editorial:
Imagine getting a dream job in Italy during the 70s, only to find out you are making sound effects for a movie that feels wrong. You follow a quiet British guy who spends his days in a dim studio, cutting tape and making gross noises to fit a scary movie on screen. The vibe is weird and moody, making you feel like something is off from the very first minute. You spend most of the time just watching him work, but the sounds start to mess with his head, and you start to wonder if the movie he is editing is actually real or just a trick of the mind.

The acting is great because it relies on small looks rather than big speeches. You will love how the sound design makes you feel uneasy, though some might find the slow pace a bit boring at first. If you like mysteries that make you think, you should definitely give this a try. It is the kind of film that works best when you turn the lights off and crank up the volume.
endingExplained: You find out the main character is not just a sound guy, but a man trapped in a loop of his own guilt. The scary movie he is editing is actually a memory of a crime he committed years ago. In the end, he realizes he has been trying to erase his past by editing the sounds. He eventually breaks down as the fake movie world and his real life crash together, leaving him broken and lost.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological puzzles and old school horror vibes.
